 Ariana Arseneault Brings Career Year into Billie Jean King Cup Play-offs
 By Francesco Tosini
 November 12, 2026
 Cheer for Canada 
 Billie Jean King Cup 
 Ariana Arseneault has had to be patient for her first Billie Jean King Cup  presented by Gainbridge match, but the 24-year-old from Richmond Hill, ON, could emerge as Team Canada’s dual threat in her third Billie Jean King Cup nomination.
 Arseneault made her first appearance at the 2025 Qualifiers in Tokyo, Japan, then was part of Canada’s most recent tie at the same stage of the competition in Astana, Kazakhstan, last April. What was consistent throughout the Richmond Hill-native’s two previous nominations was the team’s positive dynamic no matter who was a part of the squad, and Arseneault is anticipating more of the same next week in Vitoria, Brazil, as she reunites with a few familiar faces like 2026 Qualifiers teammates, Kayla Cross and Bianca Andreescu.
 “I think it’s definitely super important to have a good team dynamic, with coaches and players. We’ve been fortunate the two times that I’ve played in Japan and Kazakhstan. Everyone is super nice and accommodating,” Arseneault said in an interview on Oct. 29 in Toronto.
 It will be the first time that the 24-year-old will be in the same team as Gabriela Dabrowski, though. Arseneault added, “I’ve never really met [Dabrowski] before, so I’m super excited to get onto the court with her. I think that will be super motivational and I’ll be able to learn a lot from her.”
 Arseneault’s Billie Jean King Cup match debut could very well come alongside the two-time US Open champion. The Richmond Hillian will serve as Canada’s No. 2 in doubles and has the silverware to go along with her case to be Dabrowski’s partner in Brazil, claiming four World Tennis titles this season, with her biggest coming at the W75 Tevlin Challenger in Toronto.
 Read also: Clémence Mercier Awestruck Following First Billie Jean King Cup Nomination 
 However, Arseneault made herself one to watch in singles as well. On top of her first professional title at the W15 Trois-Rivières back in March, the world No. 337 had some strong results just last month, making back-to-back semifinals at the W50 Quebec City , then W75 Saguenay . 
 “Playing at home is always a confidence booster, and starting the indoor season was also really exciting because it’s a surface that I thrive on,” the Canadian said. “Playing a lot of matches was giving me a lot of confidence and it was a positive few weeks here [in Canada].”
 Arseneault is now hopeful of bringing that form and confidence into the Billie Jean King Cup Play-offs , where she must make the shift to clay. The 24-year-old has won three World Tennis doubles titles on the dirt, two alongside teammate Cross, as she eagerly awaits the opportunity to make more memories on clay, while donning the Maple Leaf.
 Read also: Andreescu Re-Enters Top 100 with Late Surge  
 “[Billie Jean King Cup] is always such a fun experience, being with the team and representing Canada, so I’m super excited to go to Brazil” Arseneault said. “It’s always a great time, everyone’s always excited and pumped to get the W.”
 Team Canada kicks off their tie against Brazil on Nov. 20 with two singles matches, followed by one doubles match and up to two singles matches on Nov. 21.
 Listen to the full interview with Ariana Arseneault and analysis on Tennis Canada's new podcast, the Tennis Canada News Desk.
